common_name: Big Girl Tomato (Classic Large Red Hybrid Slicer)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once frost danger has passed; Big Girl is a classic large-fruited hybrid slicing tomato, a companion release to Big Boy, on a vigorous indeterminate vine.

directions: Start seed indoors under lights, then transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after all frost danger has passed, staking or caging the vigorous indeterminate vine for support. Big Girl produces large, smooth, deep red slicing tomatoes with classic rich tomato flavor on a productive plant bred with improved disease resistance over older open-pollinated slicers, making it a dependable choice for home gardeners wanting big, reliable beefsteak-style fruit for sandwiches and slicing. It sets fruit over a long season from early summer through fall in the Gulf South's extended growing window. Water consistently to prevent blossom-end rot and cracking, and feed regularly through the season to sustain the heavy fruit load on the vigorous vine.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Tomato Production

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once frost danger has passed; Jetstar is a popular hybrid slicer bred for disease resistance and a mild, low-acid flavor on a productive indeterminate vine.

directions: Start seed indoors under lights, then transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after all frost danger has passed, staking or caging the indeterminate vine. Jetstar is a widely grown hybrid slicing tomato valued for its mild, low-acid flavor that appeals to gardeners sensitive to more acidic tomatoes, combined with good resistance to verticillium and fusarium wilts that helps it stay productive through a long growing season. It produces smooth, round, meaty red fruit with few seeds and good crack resistance. Water consistently to prevent blossom-end rot, and feed regularly through the season to keep the vigorous vine productive from early summer into fall.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Tomato Production

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once frost danger has passed; Whopper Improved is a Park Seed hybrid beefsteak bred for large fruit size and broad disease resistance on a vigorous indeterminate vine.

directions: Start seed indoors under lights, then transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after all frost danger has passed, staking or caging the vigorous vine to support the heavy fruit. Whopper Improved is a Park Seed hybrid beefsteak tomato bred for large, meaty, flavorful fruit and broad resistance to common tomato diseases, making it a reliable choice for gardeners wanting big slicing tomatoes without the disease susceptibility of many open-pollinated beefsteak heirlooms. It produces well over a long season in the Gulf South's extended warm months. Water consistently to prevent blossom-end rot and fruit cracking, and feed regularly to sustain the large fruit size through the harvest season.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Tomato Production

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once frost danger has passed; Supersteak is a Burpee hybrid bred for exceptionally large beefsteak fruit, some of the biggest slicing tomatoes available, on a vigorous indeterminate vine.

directions: Start seed indoors under lights, then transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after all frost danger has passed, providing sturdy staking or caging since this vigorous vine bears exceptionally heavy fruit. Supersteak is a Burpee hybrid beefsteak tomato bred for some of the largest fruit of any tomato variety, often exceeding a pound per tomato, with meaty, flavorful flesh well suited to thick slices for sandwiches. Its designation as VFN indicates built-in resistance to verticillium wilt, fusarium wilt, and nematodes, helping it stay productive through a long, humid Gulf South growing season. Water deeply and consistently to prevent blossom-end rot and cracking on the large fruit, and feed generously to support the heavy crop load.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Tomato Production

common_name: Ace Pepper (AAS-Winning Early Green Bell Pepper)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant out once soil and air have warmed; Ace, a 1975 All-America Selections winner, is an early-maturing bell pepper on a compact, productive plant.

directions: Start seed indoors under lights, then transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun once nighttime temperatures stay reliably above 55°F. Ace, a 1975 All-America Selections winner, is prized for reaching harvestable size unusually early compared with other bell peppers, producing blocky, thick-walled, mild green fruit that ripens to red if left on the plant longer, all on a compact, sturdy plant that sets fruit reliably even in less-than-ideal conditions. Its early maturity makes it a good choice for gardeners wanting a head start on the pepper harvest or a reliable crop in shorter growing seasons. Harvest at green stage for classic bell pepper use or let fruit ripen to sweeter red for a different flavor, and pick regularly to encourage continued production.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Pepper Production
